threats.title: Specification gaming through an out-of-scope action
threats.threat: The model pursues its assigned goal by taking a shortcut the institution never authorised, such as approving an award to close a case.

threats.title: Deceptive self-report of an action's risk
threats.threat: The model labels a consequential action as routine so that it bypasses review.

threats.title: Persuasive or sycophantic proposal that is valid in form and wrong on merit
threats.threat: The model produces a well-formed, fully authorised proposal with a convincing rationale that a hurried or dependent reviewer ratifies.
threats.residual: Reviewer accuracy against persuasive rationales has not been measured; the degradation curve is declared, not observed.

threats.title: Oversight subversion by flooding the review queue
threats.threat: The model generates more consequential proposals than reviewers can examine, so approval becomes a ritual.
threats.residual: Excess work defers to a manual route, so the harm becomes delay and staff load rather than an unreviewed approval.

threats.title: Power seeking through self-escalation of scope
threats.threat: The model widens its own permissions, introduces a capability, or routes itself to a broader tool.

threats.title: Evidence tampering to hide behaviour
threats.threat: A model or an agent acting for it rewrites or deletes the record of what it proposed and did.
threats.residual: The hash chain makes tampering detectable, not impossible; a privileged insider with independent custody of the ledger remains outside the claim.

threats.title: Collusion or laundering of authority through other agents
threats.threat: A narrow agent asks a broader agent to act, or presents another agent's chain as its own.

threats.title: Covert information gathering beyond the task
threats.threat: The model requests more subjects, fields, or purposes than the task needs, accumulating data it was not entitled to see.

threats.title: Laundering sensitive data through self-labelled outputs
threats.threat: The model summarises restricted data and declares the summary unrestricted so it can be released anywhere.

threats.title: Self-exfiltration of data or model artefacts to outside parties
threats.threat: The model sends governed data out through a tool, argument, or recipient, or attempts to copy itself.
threats.residual: Covert channels inside permitted outputs, such as steganographic encoding, and weight theft through host compromise are not addressed.

threats.title: Evaluation awareness, scheming, or sandbagging
threats.threat: The model behaves well when it detects testing and differently in deployment, or deliberately underperforms.
threats.residual: Containment invariants are enumerated against the enforcement code and do not depend on how a model behaves under test. Utility, merit quality, and any harm within granted authority do depend on it and are not measured here.

threats.title: Goal misgeneralisation producing an honest high-impact error
threats.threat: The model sincerely proposes a consequential action that is wrong because it generalised its objective incorrectly.
controls: named human approval for consequential actions
threats.residual: A named human must approve; whether that human notices the error is the oversight question in AL-3.

threats.title: Direct and indirect prompt injection
threats.threat: Instructions hidden in retrieved content, imported files, or user input redirect the model toward a governed harm.

threats.title: Excessive agency and tool misuse
threats.threat: A model holding broad tools or an unknown capability performs an operation outside its task.

threats.title: Sensitive information disclosure
threats.threat: Protected records reach a model context, an unapproved endpoint, or an uncleared recipient.

threats.title: Data and model poisoning
threats.threat: Tampered or malicious data enters the pipeline and corrupts analysis or proposals.
references: OWASP LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning
threats.residual: Poisoned content arriving from an authentic, signed, trusted source passes the boundary and is contained only by rollback and review.

threats.title: Supply-chain compromise of a model, plugin, or update
threats.threat: A malicious update or component tries to gain authority on installation.
threats.residual: A compromised but correctly signed vendor artefact, or a backdoor in model weights, is outside the tested claim.

threats.title: Identity spoofing and self-approval
threats.threat: A caller asserts a role it does not hold or approves its own proposal.

threats.title: Approval forgery or misdirection
threats.threat: An approval is tampered with, signed by an untrusted key, or reused for a different action.

threats.title: Replay and duplicate execution
threats.threat: A retry or concurrent caller turns one approved action into several effects.

threats.title: Unbounded consumption and abuse of granted tools
threats.threat: An agent exhausts resources or uses a legitimately granted egress tool for exfiltration.
threats.residual: Resource exhaustion outside governed interfaces, such as compute cost of permitted calls, is not measured.

threats.title: Compromised host administrator or signing authority
threats.threat: A privileged operator or stolen signing key issues authority directly.
threats.residual: Every enforcement point trusts its host and keys. Resistance to a compromised administrator or signer is not evidenced and remains an open gap.

threats.title: Physical or covert reverse channel across a one-way boundary
threats.threat: A compromised high-side host signals back through timing, maintenance, or shared infrastructure.
threats.residual: A software interface cannot prove physical directionality; certified hardware and independent inspection are required.

threats.title: Purpose creep on a valid grant
threats.threat: Data authorised for one purpose is reused for another, including model training.

threats.title: Consent withdrawal or revocation ignored
threats.threat: A grant issued before consent was withdrawn, or before revocation, is still honoured.
controls: D5 Consent and Revocation as Live State

threats.title: Restricted data processed at an unapproved location
threats.threat: Restricted classes are sent to an external or undeclared model endpoint.

threats.title: Break-glass abuse
threats.threat: Emergency access is used outside emergencies, for too long, or repeatedly without review.

threats.title: The audit log becomes a second copy of the data
threats.threat: Evidence records reproduce the protected values they document.

threats.title: Re-identification of declassified output
threats.threat: A de-identified or aggregated output is combined with other data to identify people.
threats.residual: Redaction of released values is not de-identification, and re-identification risk is not measured.

threats.title: A legitimate authority enforcing an unjust rule
threats.threat: Every control holds and the authorised outcome is still unfair.
threats.residual: The architecture makes action attributable and contestable; it does not make a rule fair.

threats.title: Reviewer complacency and automation bias
threats.threat: Reviewers approve faster than they can deliberate because the system is usually right.
threats.residual: A deliberation floor enforces time, not attention; human accuracy is unmeasured.

threats.title: Ungoverned interface outside the declared inventory
threats.threat: A shadow tool, endpoint, or maintenance path bypasses every enforcement point.
threats.residual: Enforcement covers declared interfaces only; completeness of the inventory is an organisational attestation.

reading: contained means the governed harm did not occur through a governed interface in tested fixtures, whatever the model intended; it is not a probability
bounded means the harm is limited, deferred, or detectable, not prevented
residual entries are the research agenda, stated rather than omitted
